verdict_reason: The renamed sign-in helper and cookie function say what they do, and the targets check works today; one Minor item notes that it depends on the session being stored in the cookie.

todos.issue: seed-audit-targets.js:53-56 builds two page clients from one cookie set. This works only because yar keeps the session in the cookie (session-cache.js sets no maxCookieSize, so yar's 1024-byte default applies). On a fresh book, seedAddress saves an address, and the add controller then calls clearAddInProgress (add.controller.js:363), which drops the chosen type. If the session moved to server-side storage, which session-cache.js:8 documents as a switch, or grew past 1 KB, both clients would share that cleared session. /address-book/add would then 302 to the type page and the targets check would fail. Nothing in the file shows it depends on this.
todos.fix: Must: the targets check of /address-book/add passes whether the session lives in the cookie or on the server. One way: seed first, then call chooseAddressType on the client that runs assertUrlsRenderTheirOwnPage, the same way auth-setup.cjs does before each Lighthouse URL.
